claims.statement: ONE SOURCE: the card's executability IS the packet's readiness — Store.readiness(id) is the single derivation (L0), consumed by both; materialize() no longer derives it. Pinned by an agreement test comparing Store.detail(id).readiness against assemblePacket(...).readiness on all four shapes (ready · unresolved input · blocking openQuestion · open DECLARED dependency), with the expected verdict pinned per case so neither side can drift.

THE READ IS PER TASK: ann detail (text + --json via TaskDetail.readiness), ann journey, the confirm card and the UI node card all print executability + its NAMED blockers for EVERY task, and the gate-queue row (ann next + the UI pending-gates drill) says what accepting would unlock. An open declared dependency reads 12/17's wording verbatim: dependency open: <id> (<status>) — never a second phrasing.

TWO QUESTIONS, TWO FACTS: detail.readiness (the engine's answer — could the frame run it now) and detail.blockers (the human's owed decision) are separate facts; a task whose only pending item is an undecided gate reads EXECUTABLE with the gate wait named beside it, and the status words are unchanged (no new word). The card renders both lines; the leg-12 grill submissions demonstrate it live.

HINTS NEVER GATE (the deadlock guard): only DECLARED edges gate. A RECIPROCAL named-in-record pair (12/12 ↔ 12/13's shape) reads executable while both hint edges stay derived and labelled named-in-record; no hint edge can make a task non-executable.

NOBODY ELSE MOVES: reads only — no new event type, no new status, no new write path. Pinned by tests: the read writes nothing (events.jsonl byte-identical after readiness/detail/lookBack), and two fixtures differing ONLY in readiness derive identical leg aggregate · ready set · leg gate · next. A leg has no executability at all (the field is absent — ready: true on a blocked leg would be the confusion this ends). The UI keeps its minimal vanilla style, no new deps.

Suite green (881 tests, 46 files), typecheck clean, ann check + ann verify clean on the live journey; the five allowlisted checks captured against faf170a via capture! (npm test · npm run typecheck · npm run build · ann check · ann verify — all PASS, source=captured), and the work committed at faf170a with structured evidence.

note:
POST-SUBMISSION CORRECTION — found by the operator's question ("why the UI didn't show any change?"), recorded BEFORE the confirm decision rather than after it.

THE TWO GAPS, both against this task's own ACs:
(1) AC-2 asks the journey and gate-queue rows to carry the same word per task. The CARD half was delivered (the node card, the pending-gates row, `ann detail`, `ann packet`); the ROW half was not. The served page's leg list, the leg tab's task buttons, `ann journey`'s task list and `ann status` still printed the bare status word — which is the one-word-two-facts this read exists to end, at the level where the walk actually starts. The cause is worth naming: the change was verified against the CARD (a probe proved the new lines render) and the rows were never re-read, so a delivery that had passed its own card tests still did not meet AC-2's row clause.
(2) AC-3's wording was wrong on an EXIT gate. The gate-queue row said "accepting it makes the task runnable" for a confirm submission too — false there: by the time confirm is submitted the work is done, and an accept CLOSES the task when the conclusion evidence is present, otherwise it leaves `complete!` owed. The first repair attempt reached for `delivered.bound`, which is NOT the right fact (it omits the `parentConcluded` clause of the auto-close predicate) and would have been a second derivation of a rule that already exists. The row now branches on `closesOnAccept`, computed from `closeEvidenceBlocker` itself — the auto-close predicate, never a re-derivation.

WHAT CHANGED (89a6bdc): `execVerdict` is printed on every TASK row — the served page's journey leg list and leg tab, `ann status` (one shared formatter in the text renderers), and the plan's per-leg task list — and on NOTHING else: a LEG carries no readiness (a leg is never run), so a leg row prints no verdict rather than an "absent means READY" reading. `TaskDetail.tasks[]`, the journey route's task rows and `Commands.statuses()` each carry `readiness` per task, all from `Store.readiness` — the ONE derivation, still. `PendingGate.closesOnAccept` drives the exit-gate sentence on both the CLI queue and the page's gate tab.

THE TWO GAPS WERE REAL AND ARE NOW CLOSED, but the row half is what AC-2 asked for and what the earlier evidence at faf170a claimed under "the journey / gate-queue rows carry the same word per task" — the claim was true of the gate queue and false of the journey rows. VERIFIED at 89a6bdc: 887 tests green (was 881; +6 for the row verdicts, the leg-row silence and the two exit rows) · typecheck clean · ann check OK (its one rule-warn is the pre-existing distance-to-goal read) · ann verify 0 drifts. LIVE: all 39 task rows carry the verdict (`12-operate-loop/04-implementation-drive-affordance blocked · executability READY` — the human owes the gate, the engine refuses nothing) and 12/18's own confirm row reads `accepting it closes the task (the conclusion evidence is present)`.
